questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content: The bond dissociation energy of B - F in BF<sub>3</sub> is 646 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup> whereas that of C - F in CF<sub>4</sub> is 515 kj mol<sup>-1</sup>. The correct reason for higher B - F bond dissociation energy as compared to that of C - F is

options.content: stronger <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.294ex" height="1ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -431 572 442" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D70E" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70E"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> bond between B and F in BF<sub>3</sub> as compared to that between C and F in CF<sub>4</sub>

significant <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="7.634ex" height="1.758ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -583 3374.4 777" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D45D" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D45D"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(503,0)"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(1298.2,0)"><use data-c="2212" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(2298.4,0)"><use data-c="1D45D" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D45D"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(2801.4,0)"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> interaction between B and F in BF<sub>3</sub> whereas there is no possibility of such interaction between C and F in CF<sub>4</sub>

lower degree of <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="7.634ex" height="1.758ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -583 3374.4 777" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D45D" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D45D"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(503,0)"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(1298.2,0)"><use data-c="2212" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(2298.4,0)"><use data-c="1D45D" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D45D"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(2801.4,0)"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> interaction between B and F in BF<sub>3</sub> than that between C and F in CF<sub>4</sub>
smaller size of B - atom as compared to that of C- atom.

questions.explanation:
In BF<sub>3</sub>, B is sp<sup>2</sup>
 hybridised and by Back Bonding method strong p<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="1ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -431 573 442" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-p<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="1ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -431 573 442" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> bond is created between filled p-orbital of F and vacant p-orbital of
B which leads to shortening of B–F bond length which results in higher bond dissociation energy of
the B–F bond. However in CF<sub>4</sub>, C does not have any vacant
p-orbitals to undergo <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="1ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -431 573 442" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D70B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D70B"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-bonding.
